prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” broker for Kansas City — the right choice depends on your needs (individual vs family vs small business vs Medicare), whether you want in-person help, and which insurers you prefer. I can, however, help you find highly qualified brokers and give a short checklist so you can pick the best one for you.

If you want me to look up specific brokers, tell me: your ZIP code and whether this is individual/family, small-group, or Medicare. I’ll pull a short list of local, licensed brokers/agencies and their strengths.

How to find a good Kansas City health insurance broker
- Use licensing/verification first: verify the agent is licensed with Kansas or Missouri insurance departments (depending on your ZIP).  
- Prefer independent brokers who represent multiple carriers (they can shop plans for you).  
- Look for relevant credentials: NAHU membership, AHIP or Medicare certification (for Medicare), ACA navigator experience (for marketplace plans).  
- Check reviews and references: Google/Yelp, BBB complaints, client testimonials.  
- Ask whether they provide plan comparisons, cost estimates (premiums + out‑of‑pocket), network checks for your doctors, prescription drug checks, and claim help after enrollment.  

Questions to ask any broker before hiring
- Are you licensed in my state (KS or MO)? Can you show your license number?  
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent or captive to one insurer?  
- How are you paid (commission, fee)? Will I be charged anything directly?  
- Do you have experience with my situation (ACA subsidies, small‑business groups, Medicare Advantage/Part D)?  
- Can you provide references from recent clients?  
- Will you help with claims and annual plan changes?  

Where to verify or find brokers
- Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance (license lookup and consumer resources).  
- NAHU “Find an Agent” tool and HealthCare.gov navigator/broker listings (for marketplace plans).  
- Medicare.gov agent/broker lookup (for Medicare plans).  
- Local reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) for service quality.

Red flags
- Refusal to disclose license or compensation.  
- Pushy sales tactics or unwillingness to show plan comparisons.  
- No willingness to help with claims or annual renewals.

If you give me your ZIP code and what type of plan you need (individual/family, small business, Medicare), I’ll find and summarize 3–5 well-rated local brokers and note their specialties and how to contact them.
